newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CBA says higher bad debts likely.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CBA says higher bad debts likely.

text.p: The Commonwealth Bank of Australia said on Tuesday higher bad debt charges were likely to rise in future results.
"I would say so on the normal cyclical patterns," CBA managing director David Murray told a news conference when asked if it was likely bad debt charges would rise in future results.
CBA's bad and doubtful debts charge fell 25 percent to A$43 million in the six months to December 31 from A$56 million in the second half of 1995/96 and A$57 million in the first half of 1995/96.
"I still think that we do have a cyclically low number there," Murray said, referring to the latest first half result.
"I think in a normal period the inflow of troublesome assets would hold up, but I don't think that the writebacks would remain as strong as they have been for the last few periods," he said.
"On that basis I believe that our normal charge would be somewhat higher than the figures we produced in the recent series of accounts," he said, referring to future results.
